newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-ESTONIA AND SCOTLAND TO REPLAY WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ESTONIA AND SCOTLAND TO REPLAY WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: Estonia and Scotland, whose World Cup qualifying match was abandoned after three seconds on October 9, must replay the match, FIFA announced on Thursday.

World soccer's governing body said the group four match, abandoned after Estonia failed to turn up for the kickoff which had been re-arranged because of inadequate floodlighting, must be replayed in Tallinn by March 16.

The match will be played in daylight and Scotland's costs of a second trip to the Baltic state will be borne by FIFA. FIFA's disciplinary committee will announce on November 23 whether or not Estonia will face sanctions for their failure to play the original game.

One player immediately affected by Thursday's decision is Scotland skipper Gary McAllister of Coventry City whose one-match ban will now be served when Scotland play Sweden in Sunday's qualifier in Glasgow.

FIFA's decision means their provisional ruling -- that Scotland be awarded the match 3-0 on default -- no longer applies. As it stands, Sweden remain top of the group with six points from three matches with Scotland in second place with four points from two games.

FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter explained FIFA had taken their decision after examining detailed documents from Estonia and that "because at no time could it be said that Estonia wilfully failed to show up for the match".

"After the original kick-off time was changed because of the problems with the floodlights, Estonia did everything they could to get the match kick-off re-organised, but simply could not do it in time," he said.

"It is in the spirit of maintaining the sporting interest of the group that it was decided to re-arrange the game. Estonia only received a fax from FIFA at nine o'clock in the morning that the match should kickoff at three that afternoon and there was not time for them to do everything they had to do."

FIFA vice-president David Will of Scotland, a member of the 1998 World Cup organising committee who made the decision, was asked to leave the committee room while the matter was discussed and said afterwards: "I am very disappointed for Gary McAllister, he seems to be the innocent victim in this.

"I am resigned to the committee's decision and I am obliged to accept it, although I cannot say I am entirely happy with it. The one thing that does surprise me is that the match is going ahead in Tallinn and not being played at a neutral venue."
